transcript.content: Hello, what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... people can actually see it, you know? Like, I'm either moving like I’m underwater, taking forever just to answer a question or even just getting out of a chair. It’s heavy. Or else I’m doing the complete opposite, pacing my apartment back and forth, rubbing my hands together like I’m trying to shake off a bad call. Which happens a lot, honestly. Just yesterday I had this lady screaming at me about a refund for a blender she bought three years ago. Three years! Who expects a refund after that long? She kept saying it was a defect, but I could hear her dog barking in the background, this tiny, yappy thing, and it just made me think about how much I wanted a dog when I was a kid. A golden retriever, specifically. But my mom was allergic, so we had fish instead. Fish are so boring. You just watch them swim. Anyway, yeah, I'm either barely moving or I can't stop.
Have you had a distinct period when your mood was unusually elevated or irritable compared with your usual self?

Elevated? Um, no, not really. I don't get super happy or, like, energized like that. I mean, I guess if I drink too much cold brew I get a little wired. There's this place near my apartment with a green awning, and their coffee is just... it's aggressive. I got a large one on Tuesday and I was practically vibrating at my desk. Plus, the barista wrote the completely wrong name on the cup. I don't even know how you hear 'Bort' when I'm standing right there. Who is named Bort? It reminds me of that old cartoon, you know the one with the license plates at the theme park? I used to watch that show all the time with my roommate back when I was taking classes. We had this terrible tiny TV that you had to smack on the side to fix the color... wait, what were you asking? Oh, irritable. I mean, callers make me annoyed, obviously, but I don't have like... days where I'm just mad or hyper for no reason.
Have you ever felt unable to move or speak even though you wanted to?

Unable to move? Um, not like paralyzed, I don't think. But when I get really overwhelmed, especially after a bad shift on the phones, I do this weird thing where I sometimes catch myself just standing in the kitchen with my coffee mug halfway to my mouth. Like I just paused in the middle of a movie frame. Or I'll find myself walking the exact same little loop by the couch over and over for no real reason. 

Which reminds me, I really need to get a new couch. The springs on the left side are completely shot because my old roommate used to sleep there every time he locked himself out of his bedroom. Which was like, at least twice a month. He had this terrible habit of leaving his keys inside his mini-fridge. I still don't understand why he was opening the mini-fridge right before leaving the apartment... maybe he was grabbing a string cheese? String cheese is actually pretty great, especially the pepper jack ones, but you have to peel them right. If you just bite into it, you're a monster. But yeah, he totally ruined the cushions, so now if you sit on that side you just sink straight down into the wood frame. It's terrible for my posture. I was looking at this nice gray sectional online, but the shipping fees are just an absolute scam at this point. 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, moving. Yeah, I just kind of freeze with my coffee or do that weird pacing loop by the ruined couch when my brain gets too full.
Have you heard voices when no one else was present?

Voices? Like, people talking to me when I'm alone? Um... well, yeah, actually. It's mostly work stuff, though. Like, my laptop will be completely shut, right? I'm off the clock, no phone ringing, but I'll hear that little *beep* from my old headset. Or I'll hear this voice, it sounds exactly like my old supervisor, Dave. He used to wear these terrible patterned ties, like, golf clubs and little sailboats. Who wears a sailboat tie to a call center? Anyway, I'll hear him say my name, or just... 'too slow.' 

Which is so annoying because I wasn't even slow, it's just the system would lag. Our software was from, like, 2005. It took a solid thirty seconds just to load a customer profile. And you're just sitting there, making small talk about the weather while the little wheel spins on the screen. I hate small talk. Once I asked a guy about the weather in Chicago and he spent ten minutes telling me about his gutters. Gutters! I don't even own a house, why would I care about leaf buildup? But yeah, the voice just says 'too slow' when I'm just sitting in my apartment trying to eat dinner or whatever.
When you are frozen like that, are you unable to speak?

Speak? Um, no, I wouldn't say I'm totally unable to speak. I just... I take forever to answer. Honestly, that's a big part of why I came in here. People have been pointing it out to me, saying they can actually see me moving like I'm underwater, or that it takes me forever just to get out of a chair or reply to a question. 

Moving like I'm underwater... man, I haven't been swimming in ages. There used to be this community pool near my old place, but they had to drain it because some teenagers threw a bunch of metal patio chairs into the deep end. Who even does that? Patio furniture is ridiculously expensive now. My mom bought this little bistro set for her balcony last spring and it was like four hundred dollars. For two tiny chairs and a table that barely fits a coffee cup! The table had this mosaic tile top, which sounds nice, but it was completely uneven. If you put a glass down, it would just wobble. I hate wobbly tables. I used to fold up little pieces of napkins or cardboard at restaurants to fix them, but now everywhere just has digital menus so you don't even get the cardboard drink coasters anymore to use as wedges. It's a real design flaw in modern dining. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, the freezing. Yeah, I can speak, I'm just really slow. Or else I'm doing the total opposite, where I'm just pacing my apartment and rubbing my hands together over and over, like I'm trying to physically shake off a bad call. But yeah, I'm not mute or anything.
Did these symptoms begin after you developed a new medical illness?

Medical illness? Um, no, not that I know of. I haven't been sick or in the hospital or anything like that. 

Honestly, even if I did get sick, calling out at my job is a complete nightmare. You have to log into this third-party HR portal, and it always, always glitches. They make you reset your password every thirty days, which is just excessive. Who can remember a new password with a capital letter, a number, and a special character every single month? I ran out of variations of my cat's name like two years ago. My cat's name is Barnaby, by the way. He's a tabby rescue. He has this weird thing where he only drinks water if it's moving, so I had to buy him one of those little fountain bowls. But the motor on the fountain hums so loud, it drives me crazy at night. I tried putting a towel under it to muffle the sound, but then Barnaby just started pulling the towel out and dragging it around the apartment like a security blanket. It's ridiculous, I'm basically living with a furry toddler. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, being sick. Yeah, no, I haven't had any new medical stuff happen. Just the things I've been telling you about.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Sad? Um... no, I wouldn't say I feel sad. I mean, I don't feel great, obviously, but it's not like I'm crying all day or feeling depressed. 

Though honestly, it's hard to feel anything when you're just exhausted. I feel like I'm always tired lately. I tried buying this new mattress topper a few weeks ago to see if it would help me sleep better. It was one of those memory foam ones that's supposed to have "cooling gel" infused into it. But let me tell you, it does not cool anything. I woke up sweating like I was in a sauna. And the smell! When you first take those things out of the plastic, they smell like a chemical factory. The instructions say to let it "breathe" for 48 hours, but I live in a one-bedroom apartment, where exactly am I supposed to put a giant foam rectangle to breathe? I ended up propping it up in my living room against the TV stand, which meant I couldn't even watch anything for two days. Not that there's anything good on anyway. Every streaming service just keeps canceling the shows I actually like after one season. They always end on a cliffhanger, too. It's so disrespectful to the viewers. You invest ten hours of your life into a story, and then boom, canceled. 

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, being sad. Yeah, no, I don't really feel sad or depressed most days. Just... whatever this is.
When you freeze, can someone move one of your arms or legs into an unusual position and have it stay there?

Move my arms? Um, no, nobody's ever tried to pose me like a mannequin or anything. I don't think I freeze quite like that. It's more like... when I get really overwhelmed, I'll sometimes just catch myself standing in the kitchen with my coffee mug halfway to my mouth, just stuck there. Or I'll be walking the same little loop by the couch over and over for no real reason. 

Speaking of the couch, I really need to vacuum under there. I dropped a pen the other day and when I reached under to get it, I pulled out a dust bunny the size of a grapefruit. It's embarrassing. I bought one of those robot vacuums a while back thinking it would solve the problem, but it just gets stuck on the fringe of my area rug. Every time I run it, it beeps frantically after five minutes like it's dying, and I have to go rescue it. It completely defeats the purpose of an automated vacuum if I have to babysit the thing. Plus, Barnaby hates it. He arches his back and hisses at it like it's a predator. I thought cats were supposed to ride around on those things—you see those videos online all the time—but no, my cat acts like it's the Terminator. I should probably just sell it online, but dealing with those marketplace apps is such a hassle. People always message you asking if it's still available and then just ghost you. Or they ask you to deliver a twenty-dollar item across town in rush hour traffic. 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, the freezing thing. Yeah, no one has ever moved my arms or legs around while I'm stuck like that. I just kind of pause in the middle of doing things, or pace in circles.
